title: Vikrant Massey Reveals WhatsApp, Car Number Were Leaked After The Sabarmati Report
excerpt: In a new interview, the actor recalls receiving open threats, online abuse, and having his personal information leaked following the release of the 2024 film based on the Godhra train fire.
body:
• Vikrant Massey says his WhatsApp number and car registration were leaked online after The Sabarmati Report's release, leading to open threats and sustained abuse
  • The actor's son was just six months old during the backlash, adding significant emotional strain to an already volatile situation
  • Massey took a break from acting in December 2024 to prioritize family, and has since returned to screen work with Netflix's Musafir Cafe
  • Despite the harassment, Massey says he remains proud of the film and has come to view his critics as "cowards"

Personal Details Leaked, Threats Followed

Bollywood actor Vikrant Massey has revealed that his personal information — including his WhatsApp number and car registration — was leaked online after the release of The Sabarmati Report in 2024, triggering a wave of threats and abuse that he says deeply affected him.

Speaking on Shekhar Suman's YouTube show Shekhar Tonite, Massey recalled the intensity of the backlash he faced for starring in the film, which was based on the 2002 Godhra train fire in Gujarat.

"I had to listen to a lot of abuse. My WhatsApp number was leaked. My car number was leaked. People threatened me openly."

— Vikrant Massey

A Film That Drew Fire

The Sabarmati Report, directed by Dheeraj Sarna and produced by Ektaa R Kapoor, depicted events surrounding the burning of the Sabarmati Express on February 27, 2002, in which 59 people were killed. The film drew strong reactions from different sections, with some critics describing it as propaganda while supporters called it a necessary examination of an underreported tragedy.

Massey has stood by the project. "I did a film called The Sabarmati Report, and I am extremely proud of that film," he said. "We made it on the Godhra train burning. We made it on the burning of the Sabarmati Express."

Family in the Crossfire

What made the period particularly painful for Massey was the timing. His son had been born just months before the film's release, and the actor said the convergence of professional backlash and new fatherhood took a significant emotional toll.

"My son had just been born then. He was just six months old. I was heavily impacted and I openly said this in the media," Massey recalled. The actor had previously spoken about how his child's name was dragged into the threats, with his family being targeted alongside him.

Success, Then a Step Back

The threats came during what Massey described as the most successful period of his career. Following acclaimed performances in 12th Fail, Sector 36, and The Sabarmati Report across 2023 and 2024, the actor had gained widespread recognition — including acknowledgment from Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who watched one of his films.

But the success felt hollow. "When my son started to say 'Papa', and I couldn't be there, I would cry and think, 'I did wish for success, but at what cost?'" Massey said. In December 2024, he announced a break from acting to recalibrate his priorities.

Return to Screen

Massey has since returned to acting and was most recently seen in the Netflix series Musafir Cafe, which has been renewed for a second season. He also appears to be in talks for a role in Aamir Khan's upcoming film Lalkaara, according to industry reports.

Reflecting on the abuse he endured, Massey said his perspective has shifted. "Over time, I realised that they are all cowards and it doesn't matter to me what people talk about me. What matters is that my own people are my responsibility. I am answerable to them," he said.

The actor's experience highlights the personal cost that can accompany politically sensitive film projects in India — and the particularly acute vulnerability of public figures whose private information can be weaponized in online campaigns.
nri_angle: Highlights the personal cost of politically sensitive film projects and online harassment faced by Bollywood actors.
